name: Hadron Experimental Facility, J-PARC
notes: Precise, building-level coordinates for the Hadron Experimental Facility were not found in any officially fetchable source this session; the j-parc.jp Hadron Facility overview page loaded but its descriptive/location text was not present in the fetched excerpt beyond a floor-plan image reference. The point recorded is the general J-PARC-site geocoder centroid also used (independently) by the japan-neutrino lead's site:j-parc-main-ring record; it does not distinguish the Hadron Hall's real position (south of the Main Ring) from the rest of the campus.

summary.plain: The building at the J-PARC laboratory in Japan where COMET (and other experiments) search for a muon turning directly into an electron, using an intense beam of muons from J-PARC's 50 GeV proton synchrotron.
summary.technical: Hadron Experimental Facility (Hadron Hall) at J-PARC, Tokai-mura, Ibaraki, fed by the 50 GeV Main Ring slow-extracted beam; hosts COMET Phase-I among other hadron/kaon experiments. No building-specific sourced coordinate was found this session; recorded as a campus-level approximate point shared in form with the existing J-PARC main-ring site record.
